sections.h2: Where is Myrtle Beach, SC, and what kind of city is it?
sections.html:
Myrtle Beach is a resort city in Horry County in the northeast corner of South Carolina, at the center of the 60-mile Grand Strand. It sits 94 miles northeast of Charleston and 74 miles southwest of Wilmington, North Carolina, and the Intracoastal Waterway has separated it from the mainland since 1936.

The figures come from the city's Wikipedia entry, apart from the 2025 estimate, which matches the Census Bureau number shown above on this page. With a median age near 50, many owners here are retirees and second-home holders, and that shapes who sells and why.

sections.h2: How does tourism shape the Myrtle Beach housing market?
sections.html:
Tourism is the main economic driver, and it creates a large pool of short-stay housing next to year-round homes. The city entry reports more than 20 million visitors a year, about 425 hotels, and roughly 1,800 to 1,900 restaurants, though its own golf course counts vary between 80 and 100.

Several large projects have changed how neighborhoods are used:

  • The Myrtle Beach Convention Center opened in 2003 and Coastal Grand Mall in 2004.
  • The Boardwalk opened in 2010 and the 200-foot SkyWheel in May 2011.
  • The Market Common was built on the former Air Force base site.
  • Grand Strand Medical Center is a 369-bed hospital with a Level 1 Adult Trauma Center, and Horry County Schools, serving about 40,000 students, is also a major employer.

A house near a tourist corridor may earn more as a rental, but a house in a quiet residential area faces different rules, which the next section covers.

sections.h2: Can I rent out or sell a Myrtle Beach house that has been a short-term rental?
sections.html:
A Myrtle Beach house can be rented for less than 90 days only if it sits in a zone that allows it. The city defines a short-term rental as any rental of under 90 days, and says most traditional residential neighborhoods do not permit them. Any zone name starting with R is excluded, except RMV (Residential Multifamily Visitor).

The city's notice adds several rules that affect a sale:

  • Renting a property requires a business license.
  • Fewer than 30 houses in traditional residential zones are exempt because they were used as short-term rentals before the current zoning.
  • A property outside a permitted zone cannot be converted to or approved for that use.
  • A violation of the zoning code or business license ordinance is a misdemeanor, with fines of up to $500, 30 days, or both.

If you are selling a house that someone has been renting by the night, confirm its zone with the city Zoning Division at 843-918-1179 before you tell a buyer it can continue. A cash buyer will ask the same question, and it affects what the house is worth to them.

sections.h2: What weather and hurricane history should Myrtle Beach sellers know?
sections.html:
Myrtle Beach has a humid subtropical climate with about 53.56 inches of precipitation a year, and September is the wettest month. Summer highs run 83 to 91 degrees. Winter lows sit in the mid to upper 30s, the city averages 33 frost days a year, and snow is rare.

Hurricane Hazel in 1954 was the worst storm in the city's history, and Hugo in 1989 was the last hurricane to cause significant damage there. In Hugo's case, Horry County took about $944 million in damage, according to the storm summary, which also quotes NOAA blaming the wind damage on underdesigned and marginal building practices. Beach erosion was severe in Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach.

For a seller, this means roof age, wind-rated windows and flood coverage are common questions from buyers and insurers. We do not have an official Horry County flood-zone figure for the city, so ask the county or city floodplain office about a specific address.

sections.h2: How do roads, the airport and neighborhoods affect where buyers look?
sections.html:
U.S. 17, the U.S. 17 Bypass, U.S. 501, SC 31 and SC 73 (Ocean Boulevard) are the main roads listed for Myrtle Beach. Myrtle Beach International Airport is county-owned and about 3 miles southwest of downtown, on the old Air Force base site. Coast RTA runs public transit, and a 14.1-mile Waccamaw Coast Line Railroad freight line connects Conway and Myrtle Beach.

The city entry names these neighborhoods:

  • Arcadian Shores, Carver, Chestnut Hill and Dunes Cove
  • Forest Acres, Grande Dunes, Harlem and Myrtle Heights
  • Myrtlewood, Ocean Forest, Pine Lakes and Seagate Village
  • Springmaid Beach, Withers Swash and Yaupon Circle

Oceanfront and golf-course areas draw different buyers than inland streets. A seller in Carver or Pine Lakes will see different comparables than one in Grande Dunes, so ask for sold prices from the same neighborhood and not the whole city.

sections.h2: How do Horry County property taxes work for a Myrtle Beach homeowner?
sections.html:
Horry County assesses and bills Myrtle Beach property. A qualified legal residence is assessed at 4 percent of fair market value, and other real property is assessed at 6 percent, so a second home or rental pays more. The formula is market value times the assessment ratio times the millage rate, and the county's FAQ shows the 2023 combined county, school, fire and waste rate was 216.2 mills before municipal charges.

Key points from the Assessor's guide:

  • Horry reassesses every four years, taking effect in the fifth. The most recent valuation date was December 31, 2023.
  • The 15 percent cap on value increases does not apply in the year a sale first becomes taxable.
  • Owners have 90 days from a reassessment notice to appeal in writing, and the Assessor's office is at 1301 2nd Avenue in Conway, phone 843-915-5040.
  • If you move, the new home needs a fresh legal residence application, and a change of use must be reported to the Assessor within six months.

State law sets the due date at January 15, with 3 percent, then 7 percent, then 5 percent penalties after that, according to the state code. Horry's Auditor can be reached at 843-915-5051.

sections.h2: How is a Myrtle Beach deed recorded?
sections.html:
Deeds for Myrtle Beach property are recorded at the Horry County Register of Deeds, 1301 Second Avenue, Conway, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. The phone is (843) 915-5430.

Recording charges for most documents became flat fees on August 1, 2019, replacing per-page charges. The amounts are listed in a fee schedule on the county's site. The deed transfer fee is separate: the state sets it at $1.85 per $500 of value, made up of $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county, and a value affidavit accompanies the deed.

Disclosure rules also apply. South Carolina requires owners to hand a buyer a written property condition statement unless the transfer is exempt, and the law allows as-is agreements. The text is in Title 27, Chapter 50.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale a fit for a Myrtle Beach house?
sections.html: A cash sale is worth a look if the house needs work, was rented hard, or belongs to heirs who live elsewhere. Cash Home Buyers reviews Myrtle Beach homes as they stand and puts any offer in writing, so you can weigh it against listing and decide on your own schedule.

faqs.q: Is Myrtle Beach in Horry County?
faqs.a: Yes. Myrtle Beach is in Horry County, and the county assessor, auditor, treasurer and Register of Deeds all handle its property records.

faqs.q: Are short-term rentals allowed in every Myrtle Beach neighborhood?
faqs.a: No. The city says most traditional residential zones do not allow rentals under 90 days, and any zone starting with R is excluded except RMV. A business license is also required.

faqs.q: What is the deed transfer fee in South Carolina?
faqs.a: It is $1.85 for each $500 of value or fraction, split $1.30 state and $0.55 county. Some transfers, such as estate distribution deeds, are exempt.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Horry County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the date you receive a reassessment notice to appeal in writing, according to the county's reassessment flyer.

faqs.q: Does selling change my Myrtle Beach property tax?
faqs.a: It can. A sale is an assessable transfer, so the 15 percent cap on value increases does not protect the new owner in the first taxable year. Ask the Assessor at 843-915-5040 how it applies.

faqs.q: When did Hurricane Hugo hit the Grand Strand?
faqs.a: Hugo came ashore near Charleston in September 1989. Horry County still took heavy damage, about $944 million, with severe beach erosion in Myrtle Beach.
